item.title: Study Examines Emotional Impact of AI Misconduct Allegations on University Students
item.description:
Study Examines Emotional Impact of AI Misconduct Allegations on University Students

A new 2024 study has investigated the emotional impact on university students who face formal academic misconduct investigations, particularly those involving allegations of cheating via generative artificial intelligence (AI). Researchers found that these accusations often rest on unreliable AI-detection programs, leading to significant psychological distress for the students involved.

🔍 Overview

In 2024, researchers conducted a large-scale survey regarding plagiarism knowledge among university students. From a group of 771 participants representing two Australian universities, 22 students identified as having been investigated for academic misconduct. These students participated in a follow-up survey and questionnaire designed to measure depression, anxiety, and stress levels experienced during the formal investigation process.

⚙️ Key details

The study compared the psychological scores of the 22 investigated students against more than 1,000 students with no misconduct history and the psychological norms of over 2,000 Australian adults. Findings included:

  • More than 50% of students facing allegations experienced extremely severe anxiety, scoring in the top 2% of the general population.
  • Half of the students reported symptoms of severe depression during the allegations.
  • Only three of the 22 investigated students reported depression, anxiety, and stress levels within the “normal” range.
  • Students who do not speak English as their first language were found to be overrepresented in misconduct allegations, supporting research regarding international students.
  • Student distress increased when academic misconduct procedures were drawn out over a longer period.

💡 Why it matters

The findings suggest that academic misconduct procedures should not proceed when based on unreliable evidence. To prevent incorrect accusations related to generative AI, researchers suggest that universities reform assessment designs to remove opportunities for cheating. Proposed changes to assessment structures include:

  • Increased use of supervised exams.
  • Implementation of in-class demonstrations.
  • Use of student presentations.

#GenerativeAI #AcademicIntegrity #HigherEducation #StudentWellbeing

Source: New research shows students experience extreme anxiety when accused of academic misconduct

item.title: UWA Launches Researcher Development Academy to Support University Research
item.description:
UWA Launches Researcher Development Academy to Support University Research

The University of Western Australia (UWA) has launched the Researcher Development Academy (RDA), a university-wide initiative designed to integrate researcher training, leadership development, and industry engagement under a single framework.

🔍 Overview

Launched by Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Science and Innovation, Yaz Muburakai MLA, the academy aims to strengthen research excellence and societal impact. It serves over 4,000 researchers, including higher degree by research (HDR) students, early-to-mid-career researchers, senior researchers, and supervisors.

⚙️ Key Details

The academy provides an integrated framework focused on research capability, leadership, communication, and career development. Key focus areas include:

  • Training in entrepreneurial mindsets and commercialization pipelines.
  • Project management and collaborative teamwork skills.
  • Communicating research to diverse audiences.

🧩 Programs and Activities

Program/Activity Description
Research Ready Integrated training and support framework
Future Forward Professional and leadership development
HDR Supervisor Training Training for research supervisors
Bold Ideas, Better Futures Flagship series featuring industry and academic speakers

💡 Why it matters

According to Pro Vice-Chancellor (Research Training), Professor Hélène de Burgh-Woodman, the academy is a significant investment in researchers and aligns with State priorities in innovation, workforce development, and economic diversification. The academy recently hosted its first theme, “Research Futures in the Age of AI,” which explored artificial intelligence in higher education, including an international keynote by Professor James Zou from Stanford University on AI agents and scientific discovery.

#UWA #Research #HigherEducation #ArtificialIntelligence

Source: New Researcher Development Academy to strengthen WA’s future workforce

item.description:
The University of Scranton Announces Faculty Promotions and Appointments for 2026-27

The University of Scranton has announced 22 faculty promotions effective Aug. 31, 2026, alongside new leadership appointments and faculty achievements heading into the 2026-27 academic year.

📋 Faculty Promotions

The following faculty members received promotions for the upcoming academic year:

🎓 Tenure Awards

Eight additional professors were granted tenure:

  • Mehmet Bastug, Ph.D. (Cybercrime and Homeland Security)
  • Vincent Farallo, Ph.D. (Biology)
  • Spencer Galen, Ph.D. (Biology)
  • Emily Gerstle, Ph.D. (Health and Human Performance)
  • Christopher Hauser, Ph.D. (Philosophy)
  • Joseph Klobusicky, Ph.D. (Math)
  • Geng Liu, Ph.D. (Physics and Engineering)

🏛️ New Academic Leadership

WeiDong Zhu, Ph.D., joined The University of Scranton in July. Dr. Zhu previously spent 19 years at Saint Peter’s University, where he held roles including dean of the College of Arts and Sciences and interim vice president for academic affairs.

🌐 Professional Recognition

Gretchen J. Van Dyke, Ph.D., associate professor of political science, has been invited to join the Bretton Woods Committee. This international network focuses on the stability of the international economic and financial system, with membership granted by invitation based on professional achievement in economic and policy matters.
